slot.brief: V(x) given as polynomial function (e.g. ax² − bx); find electric field as function of x, locate point where E = 0, or evaluate field at a point by differentiation.

stem: The potential along the $x$-axis is $V(x)=(x^3-6x^2+9x)$ V, where $x$ is measured in metres. At which position $x>2$ m does the electric field vanish?
working:
$E_x=-\dfrac{dV}{dx}=-(3x^2-12x+9)=-3(x-1)(x-3)\ \text{V m}^{-1}$.
$E_x=0\Rightarrow x=1\ \text{m}$ or $3\ \text{m}$.
For $x>2\ \text{m}$: $x=3\ \text{m}$.

Independent check: E_x=-dV/dx=-3x^2+12x-9=-3(x-1)(x-3). For x>2, E_x=0 at x=3 m.
solution:
The electric field is $E_x=-\dfrac{dV}{dx}$.
$$E_x=-3x^2+12x-9=-3(x-1)(x-3)=0$$
Thus $x=1$ m or $x=3$ m; the condition $x>2$ selects $x=3$ m.
